transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came because work’s been getting strange for me. I’m a cashier, and at the register I keep… not doing the right thing at the right time, I guess.

Like I’ll start tapping the scanner in this little pattern instead of just scanning the groceries, or I’ll just stop with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. It’s embarrassing. The line gets quiet, and then I notice everyone looking at me.

Last week they wrote me up for it. Which is why I’m here. I mean, the scanner makes this beep that kind of gets in your head, and the drawer sticks sometimes too, but… yeah, mostly I’m getting stuck doing things that don’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing.

When you're at work and you find yourself doing things like tapping the scanner or freezing up, do you have any thoughts or feelings that seem out of place or intrusive, like something else is on your mind that doesn't fit the situation?

I don’t know if it’s a thought exactly. It’s more like I get caught in the moment wrong, you know? Like the scanner beep will happen and then my hand just starts tapping it in a pattern, and I’m not scanning the groceries anymore.

Or I’ll be at the drawer and just stop there with my hand over it, and the customer’s waiting, and I can feel the whole line sort of… there. Quiet. It’s like I’m not doing what the job needs right then.

I used to be pretty good at the register, actually. I have a bachelor’s, not that it matters for cashiering, but numbers were never the problem. It’s just this getting stuck doing things that don’t fit. Last week they wrote me up for it, so… that’s why I came in.

When you find yourself tapping the scanner or freezing up, do you feel like you have to do it a certain way or a specific number of times before you can move on, even if you don’t fully understand why?

Not really a number, no. I mean, it feels like a pattern sometimes, but I don’t think I’m counting it out like “I have to do it six times” or anything.

It’s more like I just… get caught doing it. The register is beeping, the customer’s standing there, and my hand is tapping the scanner instead of scanning their things. Or I’m over the cash drawer and I just freeze there, like my body didn’t move on to the next part.

I know it doesn’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing. That’s what got me in trouble last week, actually—they wrote me up. And then I had to go back after lunch like everything was normal, which is hard because the break room has that old vending machine that hums… sorry, I’m getting off track. But no, it’s not like a set number. It’s more that I get stuck.
Do you feel like you have to do these tapping motions or freeze up, even if you don’t want to, like there’s a strong urge or pressure inside you that makes you do it?

I don’t know if I’d call it an urge exactly. It’s not like I’m thinking, “I have to do this,” but I end up doing it anyway.

At the register I just get stuck in the wrong thing—like tapping the scanner in this pattern when I should be scanning, or my hand just kind of hovering over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. And then the line gets quiet, which makes it worse, because you can feel people waiting, like when the lights at the front of the store flicker and everyone looks up for a second—sorry.

But yeah, I don’t want to be doing it. It doesn’t fit the moment, and it got me written up last week. So it’s more like I get caught there than like I choose it.
When you find yourself doing these things at work, like tapping the scanner or freezing over the drawer, do you try to stop yourself or wish you could do something different in that moment?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I’m standing there thinking I should just scan the next item or open the drawer and hand the change back, but instead I’m… tapping the scanner, or my hand is just hanging there over the cash drawer.

I came in because it’s happening enough that I can’t just pretend it’s nothing. It doesn’t fit the moment, you know? The customer’s waiting, the belt’s still moving sometimes, and I’m stuck doing the wrong thing. Last week they wrote me up for it, which was embarrassing. I kept thinking afterward about the manager’s pen, how it clicked really loud when she was talking—sorry. But yes, I wish I could just move on and do the normal next step.

When you're stuck tapping the scanner or freezing at the cash drawer, do you notice any strange sensations or perceptions, like sounds seeming louder than they should, things looking different, or anything else that doesn't seem quite real?

Yeah… mostly sounds, I guess. Not the lights looking strange so much, although the front lights do this flicker sometimes and it makes everyone’s face look tired—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I mean, most days I hear people talking off to the side of me. Like a couple of people, just out of view. Sometimes it’s from near the stockroom, like someone calling my name, or saying I rang something up wrong. And I’ll turn to check, because it sounds real enough, but there’s nobody there. Or nobody else seems to have heard it.

That can happen when I’m already stuck at the register, and then I don’t know if I should look over or keep scanning, and then the line… you know, it just gets worse.
When you're at work or elsewhere, do you ever see things that others don’t, or feel like things around you don’t seem quite real, like you're in a dream or a movie?

I don’t really see things, no… not like people standing there or a movie or anything. The “not real” part is more with sounds, if that counts.

Most days I’ll hear what sounds like a couple people talking just off to the side of me. Like near the stockroom, or behind me where the endcap is—the cereal one was moved last month and now everyone still looks in the old place, which is annoying, sorry.

Sometimes it sounds like someone says my name, or says I rang something up wrong. And I’ll turn around to check, because it sounds real enough, but there’s nobody there. Or other people are just acting normal, like they didn’t hear anything. So… not seeing things so much. More hearing things that don’t seem to be there.
Have you ever had thoughts that other people don’t seem to understand, or believed something strongly that others tell you isn’t true?

I’m not sure… I mean, people don’t always understand what I’m trying to say, but that might be because I explain it badly. My sister says I “go around the block to get to the driveway,” which, actually, our old driveway did have this weird crack down the middle and my dad kept saying he’d fix it, but he never did.

But, um… strongly believed something that people tell me isn’t true? I don’t know. I can’t think of one like that. Sometimes I get stuck on an idea, maybe, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you ever had experiences or beliefs that you know are true, but others strongly disagree with, even when you try to explain them?

I don’t… I don’t think so? Not like something I know is true and everyone else says no. I mean, I’ve argued about things before, like at work where they put the receipt tape in the wrong drawer and then everyone says, “It’s fine,” but it’s not fine because then you’re reaching across yourself all day and your shoulder starts hurting. Mine does sometimes, especially when it’s cold.

But that’s probably not what you mean. If you mean, like, a belief-belief… I can’t really think of one. Sometimes I have trouble explaining myself and people look at me like I’ve lost the point, and maybe I have. But I don’t know that I have something like that.
Have you ever believed something strongly that you know is true, but others tell you isn’t, even after you’ve tried to explain it to them?

I guess… no, not really. I’m trying to think of something like that, but I keep coming back to regular arguments, you know? Like whether someone moved something at work or whether I told my sister something already—she says I repeat myself, but she repeats herself too, especially about her neighbor’s dog.

But something I just know is true and everyone else says it isn’t… I don’t think I have one of those. Or if I do, I’m not thinking of it right now.
Do you ever find your thoughts going in a way that feels very different from how other people think, like your mind follows a path that others wouldn’t, even if you can’t quite explain how?

Maybe… I don’t know. I mean, my mind does take the long way sometimes. Like I’ll start thinking about one thing and then it connects to something else, and then I’m talking about that instead, and people say, “What does that have to do with it?” But to me there was a connection in there somewhere.

Like just now, when you said “path,” I thought about the bus route I used to take to work, because it would go way past the store and then circle back, which always seemed backwards to me. But I guess it still got there.

So… different from other people? Maybe a little? I’m not sure if it’s different or if I just don’t explain the middle parts very well.
When you hear those sounds or voices that others don't seem to hear, do they ever happen when you're not at work, like when you're at home or somewhere else quiet?

Yeah… sometimes it’s at home too. It’s quieter there, so maybe I notice it more, I don’t know. Like I’ll be in the kitchen or sitting in the living room and it sounds like a couple people talking just off to the side, not loud exactly, more like in the next aisle at the store, if that makes sense.

At work it happens a lot, most days really—someone calling my name from the stockroom, or saying I rang something up wrong, and then I turn around and there’s nobody there. Which is annoying because I already double-check prices, especially on those coupons that never scan right. At home there isn’t a stockroom, obviously, but I still get that same kind of side-voice thing sometimes, and nobody else seems to hear it.
Have you ever believed something strongly that you know is true, but others tell you isn't, even after you've tried to explain it to them?

I don’t think so… I know you asked that before, and I’m trying to be careful with it because I don’t want to say no too fast and then remember something later.

People tell me I’m wrong about little things all the time, like whether I put the receipt tape in the drawer or left it by the register, and sometimes I’m sure I did one thing and then it turns out I didn’t. But that’s not really a big belief, right? That’s just… memory, or being tired, or being distracted because the line is backing up and someone’s trying to pay with exact change in pennies.

So, no, I can’t think of anything like that—something I know is true and everybody says isn’t. Not really.

But that’s not really a big belief, right? That’s just… memory, or being tired, or being distracted because the line is backing up and someone’s trying to pay with exact change in pennies.
